messages:
nora: Heads-up: next week (Thu 09:00 PT) we'll begin rolling out the Central CI Controller (C3). This consolidates pipeline scheduling across GitHub Actions and Jenkins jobs into one controller. Short downtime expected only for legacy cron-driven jobs. :gear:

akash: Why are we doing this now?

nora: Main reasons: predictable concurrency limits, unified retries/backoff, centralized artifact cache, and simpler cost attribution. Also helps with per-team quota enforcement.

felipe: Will repos need to change their pipeline YAML?

nora: Minimal changes. We provide a compatibility shim that translates common GH Actions steps into C3 tasks. Most repos will get an automated PR with the converted pipeline. Please review transforms, especially custom action steps.

rachel: What about secrets and credentials in workflows? Any changes to where secrets live?

nora: Secrets will migrate to the new Vault-backed store. The shim maps GH secrets to C3 vault paths. Team owners must approve migrations in the PR; we won't copy anything without explicit approval.

akash: CI runners: are we still using self-hosted runners?

nora: Yes. C3 orchestrates runners the same way but introduces a short-lived runner token flow. You'll see a new runner daemon (c3-runner) that fetches ephemeral tokens from https://ci-auth.internal/v1/token. No more hardcoded long-lived tokens.

ci-bot: Pre-rollout checklist created: c3-rollout-2026-04-02. Actions: create PRs, run conversion linter, schedule smoke runs. Assignees: @felipe @akash.

felipe: How will we handle scheduled jobs (nightly reports, backups) that currently hit the repo_dispatch endpoint?

nora: C3 provides a cron manager. We'll create a migration plan: keep legacy cron for 7 days in parallel, then flip. We will not remove legacy endpoints without notice.

rachel: Any perf/regressions expected for fast unit-test jobs? Concerned about added scheduling latency.

nora: For short jobs we offer a hot-path that bypasses the heavy scheduler and places tasks on a fast queue. Typical overhead should be <50ms for enqueue. We expect improved median queue times due to better runner utilization.

akash: What's the rollback plan if something breaks massively?

nora: Short rollback steps:
1) Pause C3 routing for the affected orgs
2) Re-enable direct GH Actions runners for those repos (we keep mapping snapshots)
3) Revert any automated PRs or leave them open but not merged
We test rollback in staging tomorrow.

rachel: How will we track costs per team?

nora: C3 emits per-run cost estimates (cpu, gpu, time) and tags runs by repo/team. We'll push a usage dashboard to the console the day after rollout.

ci-bot: Smoke test plan deployed: c3-smoke-suite v1.2 scheduled at 08:00 PT on rollout day. Tests: simple build, artifact publish, secret fetch, cron job run.

felipe: Anything teams need to do right now?

nora: Two things:
- Review conversion PRs when you get them (we'll open them in batches)
- If you use custom GH Actions or self-managed steps, list them in this thread so we can add mappings

akash: I'll also coordinate with infra to ensure the artifact cache has the right eviction policy for monorepos.

ops-bot: Notice: c3-controller v0.9.0 will deploy at 07:30 PT (preflight checks enabled).

rachel: Thanks. Please @mention me if any of the product team pipelines are in the first two batches. I'll watch critical jobs.

nora: Appreciate it. We'll post hourly updates during the rollout and a short post-rollout summary. :white_check_mark:
